title: Cap. X Arg. IV close: their opinion that strips God of election/reprobation liberty under pretext of foreseen faith/unbelief is not true — we say with Paul God does all by counsel of his will (Eph. i. 11)
pass_a_gloss: That opinion therefore of theirs is not agreeable unto truth, who under pretext of foreseen faith and unbelief plainly snatch from God the liberty of election and of reprobation; and teach that what has distributed men into elect and reprobate, that discrimination as to singular persons has contingently come to pass from antecedent and discriminated acts of men. We, if in any matter, then especially in this election and preterition, say with the Apostle that God does all things from the counsel of his will, Ephes. i. 11.
pass_b_english: So their opinion is not agreeable to truth — those who, under pretext of foreseen faith and unbelief, plainly snatch from God the liberty of election and reprobation, and teach that the discrimination which has sorted men into elect and reprobate, as to singular persons, has contingently come about from men's antecedent and differing acts. We — if in anything, then especially in this election and preterition — say with the Apostle that God does all things by the counsel of his will (Eph. i. 11).
source_text: Non est ergo veritati consentanea illorum opinio, qui electionis et reprobationis libertatem, sub praetextu praevisae fidei et infidelitatis, Deo plane eripiunt; et quod homines in electos et reprobatos dispeccati, id discriminis quoad personas singulares ex antecedaneis et discriminatis hominum actibus contingenter evenisse docent. Nos, si ulla in re, tum praecipue in hac electione et praeteritione, cum Apostolo dicimus, Deum facere omnia ex consilio voluntatis suae, Ephes. i. 11.
